title: The completion of a G-ring along an ideal is a regular ring map
statement: Let $A$ be a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] (in particular Noetherian), let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal and let $A^\wedge$ be the $I$-adic completion of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], with its canonical ring map $\iota:A\to A^\wedge$. Then $\iota$ is a regular ring map in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]: it is flat, and for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$ the fibre ring $A^\wedge\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 0AH2 (lemma-map-G-ring-to-completion-regular, line 12694; reference Matsumura, Commutative Algebra, Theorem 79); its proof uses Algebra Lemmas 00MB (completion flat), 0316 (lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian), 05GI (radical-completion), More on Algebra 07C0 (lemma-regular-local), lemma-flat-unramified, lemma-regular-permanence, Algebra lemma-completion-faithfully-flat

proof.text: Since $A$ is a G-ring it is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Hence $A^\wedge$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and $\iota:A\to A^\wedge$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat]. Moreover $I$ is finitely generated.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0AH2 (line 12704ff.), first two sentences (Algebra Lemmas 00MB, 0316)

proof.text: Since $A^\wedge$ is Noetherian, by the implication (3)$\Rightarrow$(1) of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-maximal] it suffices to show: for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'\subset A^\wedge$, with $\mathfrak m=\iota^{-1}(\mathfrak m')$, the induced map of localizations $\iota_{\mathfrak m'}:A_{\mathfrak m}\to(A^\wedge)_{\mathfrak m'}$ is regular. Fix such $\mathfrak m'$ and write $B=(A^\wedge)_{\mathfrak m'}$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0AH2 (line 12704ff.), 'it suffices to check the third condition of Lemma 07C0'

proof.text: As $I$ is finitely generated, $A^\wedge$ is $IA^\wedge$-adically complete and the map $\pi:A^\wedge\to A/I$, $(x_n)_n\mapsto x_1$, is surjective with kernel $IA^\wedge$ and $\pi\circ\iota$ equal to the quotient map $q:A\to A/I$ [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-adic-complete-jacobson-radical] to the ring $A^\wedge$ and the ideal $IA^\wedge$, the ideal $IA^\wedge$ lies in the Jacobson radical of $A^\wedge$, hence in the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0AH2 (line 12704ff.), Algebra Lemma 05GI, part (4); 'A^/IA^ = A/I' is Algebra Lemma 05GG

proof.text: For each b in the completion, choose a in A whose image in A/I equals the projection of b. Then b - iota(a) lies in the projection kernel IAhat. If b belongs to the maximal ideal mprime, then iota(a) belongs to mprime, hence a belongs to its contraction m. Since IAhat is contained in mprime, I is contained in m, and this proves mprime = mAhat. These representatives also prove surjectivity on the residue fields of the localized rings: every element of the residue field at the maximal ideal mprime is represented by b in Ahat, and then by iota(a). The localized map is local, so its residue-field map is injective. No maximality assertion about m is needed for the subsequent argument.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0AH2 (line 12704ff.), 'Since A^/IA^ = A/I we see that I ⊂ m, m/I = m'/IA^, and A/m = A^/m' ... m is a maximal ideal as well'

proof.text: Localize iota at mprime. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] this gives a flat local homomorphism phi : A_m -> B between Noetherian local rings. The equality mprime = mAhat, mapped into B and combined with the localization formula for maximal ideals [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], gives phi(m A_m) B = maximalIdeal(B). Its residue-field map is bijective by the representatives in step 4 and the maximal-ideal contraction identity for a local map.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0AH2 (line 12704ff.), 'Then A_m → A^_m' is a flat local ring homomorphism of Noetherian local rings which identifies residue fields and such that mA^_m' = m'A^_m''

proof.text: Let $(A_{\mathfrak m})^\wedge$ and $B^\wedge$ be the completions of $A_{\mathfrak m}$ and $B$ at their maximal ideals [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], with canonical maps $c_A:A_{\mathfrak m}\to(A_{\mathfrak m})^\wedge$, $c_B:B\to B^\wedge$. By Step 5 and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-completion-iso], the induced ring map $\psi=(\iota_{\mathfrak m'})^\wedge:(A_{\mathfrak m})^\wedge\to B^\wedge$ is an isomorphism with $\psi\circ c_A=c_B\circ\iota_{\mathfrak m'}$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0AH2 (line 12704ff.), 'Thus it induces an isomorphism on complete local rings, see Lemma 0AGX'

proof.text: Let e : completion(A_m) -> completion(B) be the ring isomorphism obtained in step 6, and define g : B -> completion(A_m) as the completion map of B followed by e inverse. The compatibility from step 6 gives g composed with phi equal to the canonical completion map of A_m. This composite is regular by the G-ring hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] at the prime m. Thus no transport theorem for regularity is required.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0AH2 (line 12704ff.), '... because A_m → (A_m)^ is regular as A is a G-ring'; the identification ((A^)_m')^ = (A_m)^ in the display

proof.text: The completion map of the Noetherian local ring B is flat [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]. Its composite g with the bijective ring map e inverse is flat, since bijective maps are flat and flatness is closed under composition. Both factors are local homomorphisms, so g is local. Flatness and locality imply faithful flatness, and therefore the induced map on prime spectra is surjective, using the same Mathlib faithful-flatness criterion as [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat].

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0AH2 (line 12704ff.), 'is faithfully flat (Algebra, Lemma 00MC)'

proof.text: Use phi to equip B with its A_m-algebra structure and g to equip completion(A_m) with its B-algebra structure. The commuting triangle from step 7 gives the scalar-tower identity with the canonical A_m-algebra structure on completion(A_m). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-permanence]: its regular composite is the G-ring completion map from step 7 and its flat spectrum-surjective second map is g from step 8. This proves phi regular. For every maximal mprime the same argument applies, so [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-maximal] proves the original completion map regular.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0AH2 (line 12704ff.), 'Thus we can apply Lemma 07NT to the ring maps A_m → (A^)_m' → (A_m)^ to conclude'
